text: Elaine: quick design check — I'm iterating on the bulk-invite journey for org admins. main questions: where should the SSO enforcement toggle live (invite modal vs org settings), and how do we keep audit-log navigation discoverable after batch invites? screenshots attached in original thread :mag_right: Marcos: curious — what's the tradeoff we're optimizing for? discoverability vs reducing clicks for power users? Elaine: both. product goal is fewer friction points for org admins onboarding lots of seats, but security/compliance wants SSO clearly visible and audited. current mock puts SSO toggle inside the invite modal header (right side). that felt terse. Priya: a11y note — putting the toggle inside a modal header makes it easy to miss for keyboard-only users. Also, we need to ensure the audit link is in the modal footer and tabbable before the close button. Suggested: move SSO toggle to a static row in org settings and add a read-only indicator in the invite modal that links to the setting. Sam: code-wise the indicator can be a small badge with role="status" + an anchor to /orgs/:orgId/settings/sso. Example: ``` SSO enforced ``` that keeps modal simple and avoids mounting complex toggles in the invite flow. Marcos: UX trade — if it's read-only in the modal, admins might expect to change for a one-off invite. Do we want to support an inline opt-out? legal said no. Elaine: legal and security want SSO enforcement at org level, no per-invite override. so inline opt-out isn't allowed. we need to make that clear in the copy. Priya: suggested copy for the badge: "SSO enforced — managed at Organization settings". Add an aria-describedby pointing to a hidden region that explains why. Also color contrast on the badge should meet AA (min 4.5:1 for normal text). Marcos: noting microcopy options — alternative shorter: "SSO enforced (org)" vs longer explanatory. I prefer slightly longer but not a full sentence. Sam: implementation nit — if we link to settings, use a deep link that opens Settings in the console and highlights the SSO panel (prefers anchor + focus management). We can implement a query param like ?focus=sso to highlight and focus. Elaine: good. UX followups: 1) Put badge in invite modal header left of title, 2) Add small info icon that opens a tooltip with the copy Priya suggested, 3) Make audit-log quick link in footer that goes to /orgs/:orgId/audit?filter=invites and opens in the same tab. Marcos: quick layout mock attached — header badge + tooltip. Also proposing to reduce header density: move org selector down so badge doesn't feel cramped. Priya: accessibility checklist: keyboard focus order tested, tooltip accessible via keyboard (enter/space), tooltip content in DOM (not CSS-only), role="dialog" for the modal and aria-modal="true", and provide skip link from modal to audit link for screen reader users who might want to jump. Sam: will prototype today — questions about animation: don't animate focus changes when deep-linking, needs to be instant for SR users. Elaine: thanks. One copy tweak request from security: replace "enforced" with "required" in the UI (they want firm language). So copy now: "SSO required — managed in Organization settings". Priya — still ok for aria-label? Priya: wording fine. prefer aria-label match visible text. Also request we include a short explanation in the audit entry: when batch invite happens, include "SSO: required" so the audit row is self-describing. Marcos: small a11y / visual note — badge size: 12px cap + 4px vertical padding looked cramped on 320px containers. increase min-width and allow wrap. Sam: noted. I'll PR a prototype with HTML + CSS + simple focus management. Will add test plan for keyboard navigation + NVDA/VoiceOver checklist. DevBot: deploy queued to staging for branch feature/invite-batch-sso-badge at 2101234999 — see Elaine: perfect. if the staging build looks good, we'll run a short usability test with two admins next week. thanks all :thumbsup:
